pr.title: coverage: Avoid getting extra unexpansion info when we don't need it
pr.description:
Several callers of `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro` would immediately discard the additional macro-related information, which is wasteful. We can avoid this by having them instead call a simpler method that just returns the span they care about.

This PR also moves the relevant functions out of `coverage::spans::from_mir` and into a new submodule `coverage::unexpand`, so that calling them from `coverage::mappings` is less awkward.

There should be no actual changes to coverage-instrumentation output, as demonstrated by the absence of test updates.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: PR #127157 is an explicitly behavior-preserving coverage refactor: callers that discarded the visible-macro symbol now call `unexpand_into_body_span`, which delegates to `find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt`. The old manual walk returns the same `curr` span (indeed its debug assertion enforces `curr == find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt(body_span)`), so the two paths are semantically equivalent. The frozen analysis itself states the historical transformation is not shown to be semantically incorrect, and the PR claims no coverage-output changes. There is no source-grounded wrong transformation to encode, and inventing one would be an unrelated rewrite.

evidence: Several callers of `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro` would immediately discard the additional macro-related information, which is wasteful.
There should be no actual changes to coverage-instrumentation output, as demonstrated by the absence of test updates.
+    // Because we don't need to return any extra ancestor information,
+    // we can just delegate directly to `find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation is not shown to be semantically incorrect. It optimized an inefficient path by replacing `let (span, _) = unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro(...)` at branch/MC-DC call sites with `let span = unexpand_into_body_span(...)`, where the new helper directly returns `original_span.find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt(body_span)`. The older code correctly returned the span but performed unnecessary ancestor tracking and macro-kind inspection whose result was immediately discarded. The reusable correctness invariant is that dropping the visible-macro computation must not change the selected span or the `None`/`Some` behavior.
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage instrumentation (`InstrumentCoverage`) extraction of mapping spans for branch pairs, MC/DC decisions, and MC/DC decision spans from MIR. Raw spans may originate inside macro expansions; callers reject spans whose outer expansion context is not root, then map the span back into the function body's syntax context. `body_span` supplies both the containment boundary and the target syntax context.
analysis.originalLogic: The full helper returned `Option<(Span, Option<Symbol>)>`: it walked expansion ancestors via `parent_callsite`, tracked the previous ancestor, and inspected that ancestor's `outer_expn_data().kind` for `ExpnKind::Macro(MacroKind::Bang, name)` to produce a visible macro name. Callers in branch/MC-DC mapping extraction used only the span component. The manual walk was: `while !body_span.contains(curr) || !curr.eq_ctxt(body_span) { prev = Some(curr); curr = curr.parent_callsite()?; }`, followed by debug assertions.
pitfalls: Do not replace the span computation with `find_ancestor_in_same_ctxt`: the relevant operation is `find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt`, which also enforces containment in `body_span`.
Keep the full `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro` helper for callers that actually need the macro symbol (the `from_mir` path).
Do not alter the call-site root-expansion guards or body-span argument while removing the discarded macro work.

The patch also changes a debug assertion from `find_ancestor_in_same_ctxt` to `find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt`; treat the API distinction as a refactoring hazard even though the stated output is unchanged.
No test updates are expected because coverage-instrumentation output is claimed to be identical.
preconditions: The caller ignores the second element of `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro`.
The original span's expansion ancestors can be walked to a span satisfying both `body_span.contains(curr)` and `curr.eq_ctxt(body_span)`.
Existing root-expansion checks at the call sites remain in force.
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage span unexpansion should compute only the information the caller consumes: branch/MC-DC mapping callers that need only the unexpanded body span should call `unexpand_into_body_span`, which delegates to `find_ancestor_inside_same_ctxt`, instead of always calling `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro` and discarding the macro symbol. The span result must remain identical; this historical PR was behavior-preserving and explicitly made no coverage-output changes.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct focused span cases and compare the two helpers directly: for each `(original_span, body_span)`, assert that `unexpand_into_body_span` returns exactly `unexpand_into_body_span_with_visible_macro(...).map(|(span, _)| span)`, including macro-expanded spans, nested bang macros, spans outside the body, and spans already in the body context. Include a case where the visible macro name differs but the span must remain the same. Then run the existing coverage UI/regression suite to confirm mappings are unchanged; this historical patch added no test updates because it claimed no output changes. Do not claim these tests were executed here.
analysis.trigger: A coverage mapping call site (e.g. `extract_branch_pairs`, `extract_mcdc_mappings`, and MC/DC decision handling) needs only the unexpanded span contained in the body span and does not consume the visible macro name.
